motion.name: terrain-scroll
motion.value: 66 internal pixels/s while driving; 0 throughout the death/rebirth sequence
motion.purpose: Road and all landscape camera travel stop together during rebirth and resume after the compact-garage exit; atmospheric UFOs continue hovering.

motion.name: mountain-parallax
motion.purpose: Distant cyan/blue mountains and their small skylines.

motion.name: foothill-parallax
motion.purpose: Near green hills and windowed cities with yellow rims.

motion.name: rover-drift
motion.value: One rover, preferred 24s cruise between 19% and 28% of canvas width; −10…12 internal pixels/s clear-road screen velocity; 54 internal pixels/s² acceleration; avoidance bounded to left 42%
motion.purpose: Gentle bidirectional screen drift keeps clear-road world progress within 56–78 internal pixels/s. Predictive hazard avoidance overrides the preference and commits safe ground-hop throttle and launch time through landing; obstacle death or a new incoming projectile cancels the plan.

motion.name: automatic-hop
motion.value: 225 internal pixels/s launch; 420 internal pixels/s² gravity
motion.purpose: Beginner reacts to nearby hazards and can jump a simple ditch; after the first death the driver rehearses takeoff, landing and future bomb craters. No opening ditch or forced crash.

motion.name: crash-recovery
motion.value: All parts rest + .35s; 2.6s growth with .045s stagger; 0.5s shutter lift + 1.8s compact-garage exit
motion.purpose: Wreckage becomes varied towers at 90% of the previous large-city size (2.7× original small towers), with one compact 44x34 garage replacing the former 60px facade. Its shutter lifts for 0.5s, then the buggy rolls out over 1.8s before scrolling resumes. Towers mix five silhouettes with no white rooftop crossbars.

motion.name: saucer-waves
motion.value: 3–5 ships from ahead; .4s stagger; 6–11s clear gap; 6 ships maximum
motion.purpose: Scouts, bombers, darts and carriers differ in speed, path and armor. All bombs fall vertically while ahead of the buggy, with 2.8–4.4s between drops. Arrivals pause during rebirth.

motion.name: wreckage-physics
motion.value: 300 internal pixels/s² gravity; .34 bounce restitution; wheel friction 45 and body friction 115 internal pixels/s²
motion.purpose: Ten recognizable buggy pieces, including the fixed upward barrel and forward cannon, fly out while scrolling is stopped. All must settle before their alien buildings can grow.

motion.name: ufo-hit-flash
motion.purpose: Brief hull flash makes multi-hit bomber/carrier armor visible.

motion.name: ground-turrets
motion.value: Singles or pairs; 1.8–3.4s within pairs, 16–32s gaps; 3.2–4.8s shots; 105px/s rounds; .13s flash
motion.purpose: Primitive deep-rust (#a04018) fixed pedestals and pipe barrels share one paint without perimeter edging and track the rover and its jumps from an 11-pixel-high pivot, with rounds originating 15 pixels along the barrel. At most three turrets/eight rounds; no targeting or new fire during rebirth.

motion.name: depth-atmosphere
motion.value: UFOs 6–8 × 3 distant / 9–12 × 4 middle; slow drift 2 × scale px/s, sway 3 × scale, bob 2 × scale
motion.purpose: Small layer-colored UFOs occasionally drop harmless vertical bombs with brief ground flickers. No foreground damage, visible bullet hits or city growth. Pause freezes everything.

motion.name: fixed-paired-fire
motion.value: 0.22s shared trigger; 320 pixels/s; maximum 3 airborne pairs (6 rounds)
motion.purpose: The fixed up and forward cannons fire together. A burst slot remains occupied until both rounds are gone. No swivel or independent cannon state.

motion.name: city-ground-fill
motion.value: 18px foundation margin; one 24-spark blast per reached hazard; holes fill with foundation growth easing
motion.purpose: Only growing foreground cities blast nearby turrets, rocks and holes. Rocks/turrets disappear regardless of armor; holes fill into solid ground and building bases rise. Distant hazards remain; later bombs can reopen ground.

tireShade.rule: Round each body sRGB channel multiplied by the factor; all tires share that darker hue.

buggyPalette.rule: Hot magenta, scarlet, electric violet and orange stay bright and saturated without outlines. Tires use the darker body hue; exclude blue/cyan/green landscape paints.

cityArchitecture.rule: Stable fragment/generation styles and world-tile variation; no white roof bars. Garage stays 44x34 to retain buggy clearance.

narrative.overview: A self-playing pixel arcade patrol follows the user’s Moon Patrol reference: open black sky, cyan mountains with blue facets, green foothills, peach ground, and one small buggy whose body hue and darker matching tires change with each generation. Original procedural sprites and stepped silhouettes keep the artwork self-contained. This design system applies only to this piece.
keyCharacteristics: Saturated flat fills and whole-pixel edges.
Cities mixed into both landscape layers, three scrolling speeds, and one rover that drifts forward and back.
Automatic hops, synchronized upward/forward burst fire, distinct UFO formations and attacks.
Death stops landscape scrolling while wreckage grows into buildings and a compact garage releases the next rover; atmospheric UFOs keep hovering.
A text-free full-viewport canvas with accessible pause and export.

rules.name: The Hard-Pixel Rule
rules.body: Use flat palette fills and whole-pixel scan conversion; no smoothing, gradients, or glow.

dos: Do preserve the open black sky, saturated landscape layers, and readable rover separated from the landscape by its paint rather than an outline.
Do blast hazards near growing foundations once, fill affected holes, and preserve hazards outside that reach.
Do retain keyboard access, reduced-motion pause, and dependency-free rendering.
donts: Don’t draw titles, scores, labels, controls, or a top bar over the artwork.
Don’t add a repair saucer, downward repair shots, a moon, orchard growth, or saved scene state.
Don’t introduce smoothing, glow, gradients, or interface panels.
